assessments.reasoning: The five contiguous parts of SPDX’s json/details/CC-BY-4.0.json cover 80,645 bytes, SHA-256 7f491767f9b40149851f17a0009605d2734c61a76dfa43f7a8fff055bf999925. Part 1 gives isDeprecatedLicenseId=false and the BY 4.0 International licenseText. Part 3 gives the exact name, licenseId and both publisher citations.

The GitHub API for spdx/license-list-data gives annotated tag object 76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b, named v3.29.0, targeting object type commit with SHA 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48. This is the detail-file commit. The API reports the tag unsigned.

As context, the publisher response at the exact cited URL has the scoped SHA-256 5edfcb0fd293bc651d2600940a296721a0a92a4e1adba9228e54e69a25e28848 and names BY 4.0 International inline. SPDX supplies the membership evidence.

challenge.method: Checked the tag object’s target against the commit in the detail-file URL. Compared the BY identifier and both source fields with the NC record and tested whether the crossRef match flag or differences in section numbering contradicted the citation.
challenge.results: The BY record cites /by/4.0/legalcode, while the NC record cites /by-nc/4.0/legalcode. BY crossRef.match is the string “false.” SPDX licenseText letters the remedies paragraph 6(c), while the publisher places it within 6(b). Both observations matter to a text comparison. Neither changes the recorded identifier or URL.

limitations: The correspondence is an identifier and URL citation in one generated record. It establishes neither semantic equivalence nor a grant, interpretation, translation, adaptation or redistribution right for any project file.
The live publisher capture declares /legalcode.en canonical. Its measured digest applies only to the captured /legalcode representation.
SPDX deprecation and release membership are scoped to the tagged data. Index maintenance and publisher currency are separate questions.
